name: JAPAN

flag.title: The Hinomaru
flag.note: a red sun on white · official since 1999

lead: Japan is an island country in East Asia, near Korea, China and Russia. People call it Nihon or Nippon, which means “sun origin”. That is why it is nicknamed the Land of the Rising Sun.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Japan is an archipelago, a chain of thousands of islands. Four big ones hold almost everybody: Honshu (with Tokyo, the capital), snowy Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku.

Mount Fuji is the tallest peak, at 3,776 metres. It is a volcano, but it has not erupted since 1707. Japan sits on the “Ring of Fire”, a ring of volcanoes around the Pacific. Earthquakes and hot springs are common.
animals: In the Nagano mountains, Japanese macaques (snow monkeys) climb into steaming hot springs to keep warm.
In Nara Park, more than a thousand sika deer roam free. Some bow their heads to ask for crackers.
culture: In spring, families picnic under pink cherry blossom (sakura). This is called hanami. Sushi, ramen, and bento (lunch) boxes are loved everywhere. Japan also gave the world origami (paper folding), manga (comics), and anime.
Sumo is the oldest national sport. Two huge wrestlers push each other out of a ring, and a match can end in seconds. Baseball is the most popular game to watch.
history: From the 1100s to the late 1800s, samurai guarded Japan. They were warriors famous for their swords and a code of honour called bushido.
Japan still has an emperor, but he mostly takes part in ceremonies and does not run the country. Its line of emperors is one of the oldest in the world.
wows: Snow monkeys are the only wild monkeys known to take hot baths.
The Hayabusa bullet train runs at 320 km/h and arrives on time to the second.
The world’s oldest company, Kongō Gumi, built temples for over 1,400 years.
The world’s oldest hotel is a hot-spring inn open since 705 AD.
Square watermelons are real: ordinary melons grown inside box-shaped moulds.
Japan has around 2.6 million vending machines, about one for every 23–30 people.
Capsule hotels, where guests sleep in tiny stacked pods, began in 1979.

myths.myth: Ninjas wore all black and had magic powers
myths.fact: Real ninjas were spies who dressed like farmers and travellers. The black outfit came from stage plays.
Sushi means vinegared rice. Raw fish alone is called sashimi.
